decided: Under the program sign-off, a program counts as finished when every stage its doc declares is complete, ended, or has all its work archived and waits for its completion to be confirmed. That widens D-ps-5's every declared stage archived only by counting an ended stage, and only under the program sign-off. The program counts as done, so that the user is asked to sign, once it is finished and an architecture review of the doc has been recorded after the last of its changes was archived. Each sign-off records which closing review it was given under; running that review again over the same work leaves the signature standing, and only a change of the program archived after it has the user asked afresh.
alternatives: let the architect session judge both conditions itself, as it judges the program PR's readiness today
order a sign-off against the closing review by the time each was written
why: Orbit, not the session, then decides when the user is asked, so a test can hold it. The sign-off and the review are recorded in separate places whose times cannot be reliably compared, so the sign-off names its closing review rather than leaving it to be worked out from when each was written.

defines.definition: a stage the user declared over without meeting its exit criteria, marked in the doc
